user: Ball detection (detect_ball) runs ~1.9x faster and the web UI progress bar now advances during it instead of freezing
what: detect_ball's SAHI slice count cut from 15 to 6 per 1080p frame (slice_size 512→768) and a throttled per-frame progress callback (stage "detect_ball") threaded through state.progress so the web UI bar advances every ~20 frames
why: detect_ball was the heaviest per-frame stage (~258ms/frame, ~8min/clip) and the only per-frame stage with no progress callback, so the UI froze during it. Larger slices needed a lower conf (0.15→0.10) to hold ball recall at the larger patch size.
next: See docs/wiki/learnings/detect-ball-slice-size-vs-ball-recall-on-1080p.md for the measured slice/recall table and the recall-preserving ceiling
summary: In voetlab/detection/detect.py: _run_sahi gained stage + throttle_every params (default keeps detect()'s every-frame emit unchanged) and a guarded final emit; detect_ball_sahi defaults slice_size 512→768 and conf 0.15→0.10, threads progress through with stage="detect_ball"/throttle_every=20; _detect_ball_feature passes state.progress. Measured on football-1.mp4 40-frame sample: 258ms→133ms/frame (15→6 slices), ball-rate 100%→98% (within 10% budget). 2-slice config (slice_size>=1280) collapses recall to ~50% so 6 slices is the floor. pytest: 109 passed, 4 skipped.

Includes diagnosis method (1-byte range GET, Server header, SPA-bundled-asset 404).
